text:
ConocoPhillips fell 0.7% today after climbing 13% over the past two weeks, pulled back by a sharp drop in oil prices. The U.S. benchmark crude fell below $102 a barrel after news that President Trump suspended new duties on Russian goods under a national-interest waiver, raising expectations that Russian oil could flow back into global markets and ease supply concerns that had been driving prices higher. The company had benefited from the recent spike — US oil had jumped from around $138 to $147 in just four days — so a pullback in the commodity itself is the most direct explanation for today's decline.

The broader picture remains mixed. While geopolitical tensions (Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, Iranian military posturing) continue to threaten Middle Eastern supply, the possibility of Russian crude returning to the market is offsetting those risks for now. Oil prices are still well above where they stood two weeks ago, so the underlying bullish backdrop for an oil producer remains intact, but today's supply relief story outweighed that tailwind.
